key_findings: Extreme rainfall events (>100mm/day) have increased by 350%
Maximum daily rainfall intensity has increased by 14%
Extreme events in the last decade (5) are significantly higher than the first decade (1)

flood_risk_factors.summary: Environmental changes have moderately increased flood vulnerability

factors.description: Forest cover reduced from 36.3% to 34.0% (6.3% loss)
factors.explanation: Less forest = reduced water absorption = more surface runoff during heavy rain

factors.description: Population density increased from 275 to 356 people/sq.km (29.3% increase)
factors.explanation: More people = more infrastructure = more impervious surfaces = more flood exposure

factors.description: Urban population increased from 16.3% to 20.3% of total
factors.explanation: Urban areas have concrete/asphalt surfaces that prevent water absorption

flood_risk_factors.recommendation: Reforestation in catchment areas can reduce flood peaks by 20-30%; Improved drainage infrastructure needed in high-density areas; Permeable surfaces and urban green spaces can mitigate urban flooding
